session_dialogue.text: Hello. How are you feeling today?
I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed, but I'm trying to stay strong. It's been a tough week with everything going on.
I'm sorry to hear that. You're doing really well by trying to stay strong—don't forget to take care of yourself too.
Thank you. I know I should, but it's hard when everything feels like it's falling apart. I keep thinking about how much I'm letting people down.
It's okay to feel that way. You're not alone in this, and it's completely normal to feel like you're letting others down when things get overwhelming.
I just feel like no matter how hard I try, I can't seem to make things right. I keep trying to help everyone, but I don't feel like I'm enough.
You're not failing—what you're describing sounds a lot like caring too much, and that's not a bad thing. It just means you're deeply connected to the people around you.
I guess... I just wish I could be enough for everyone without feeling like I'm failing. I feel like I'm always trying to fix things, but nothing ever seems to work out.
It’s understandable to feel that way, but you’re not failing—you’re just carrying a lot. Let’s work on finding some balance together.
I don’t know how to stop trying to fix everything. I feel like if I don’t help, no one will. But I’m so tired of always being the one who has to fix things.
You’re not alone in feeling that way, and it’s okay to feel overwhelmed. Let’s explore what it would look like to take a step back without losing your sense of purpose.
I don’t know where to start. I feel like if I stop helping, I’ll be letting people down. But I’m so tired of always being the one who has to fix things.
You’re not letting anyone down by taking a break—you’re giving yourself permission to heal. Let’s find small ways to shift the balance, even if it feels uncomfortable at first.
I don’t know if I can do that. I keep thinking about how much I’ve helped others, and I feel like I’m not doing enough. I’m scared I’ll lose their trust if I stop.
You’ve done so much already, and it’s okay to need a pause. Trust is built over time, and it doesn’t mean you’re not enough—it means you’re human.
I just don’t want to feel like I’m not enough. I keep trying to prove myself, but no matter how hard I try, I still feel like I’m failing.
You’re not failing—you’re simply trying to be enough, and that takes courage. Let’s focus on what you’re already doing right, rather than what you feel you’re missing.
I don’t know what I’m doing right. I feel like I’m always trying to fix things, but nothing ever seems to work. I just want to feel like I’m enough.

You’re not broken, and you’re not failing—you’re just trying to be enough in a world that often asks for more than you can give. Let’s start by acknowledging what you’re already doing, even if it feels small.
I don’t see anything I’m doing right. I just feel like I’m always trying to fix things, but nothing ever seems to work. I just want to feel like I’m enough.
